ICE had no clear legal obligation to publish any of this. Congress dropped the longstanding transparency requirement, and the agency went dark for months. I do not know why ICE released the data now. If you have any idea, tell me.

So how are people getting out if not by deportation? A category that did not exist a year ago answers part of it. "Court ordered" releases have climbed to about 2,000 a month and now make up roughly 1 in 4 of all non-deportation releases.

The largest group in ICE detention is now people with no criminal record. Among those ICE itself arrested, the share with a conviction fell from about 65% of detainees in 2024 to 31% today, while the share with no record rose from about 6% to 37%.

Deportations have not kept pace with the arrest surge. ICE removed people at about 1,246 a day from early April to early July, down from roughly 1,370 a day in February. Arrests are climbing while the daily deportation rate drifts down.

As of July 11, ICE held 65,765 people in immigration detention. That is down from the record high of 70,766 in late January, but detention has not come down in any real way. It sits far above where ICE held people for most of the past decade.

ICE is quietly arresting more people than ever. After months of releasing no detention data at all, the new numbers show a record 1,474 arrests a day in early July, the highest daily pace of the entire Trump administration. 🧵
